References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166) and refs therein
Comments: Adjusted linework to accord with the structure contouring interpretations of Barrell and Strong 2012 (CR2012/245) . Rake revised to include dextral component. SRs from Litchfield et al.

Name: Dalgety
References: Barrell and Strong 2010 (CR2010/147); Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014
Comments: Following the discussion of Barrell 2016, the 'Longden' Holocene fault scarp is interpreted to contain the southern end of the Dalgety source, the Dalgety Fault also having some relatively young fault scarps on hillslopes. SR from Litchfield et al.

Name: Chamberlain
References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166) and refs therein
Comments: Formerly identified as part of Opawa Fault (Litchfield et al. 2013).  SR from Litchfield et al., lack of known deformation on relatively old fans and terraces is basis for slow SRs and QC of 4 in 100 ky timeframe

Name: Grampian
References: Barrell CFM compilation
Comments: Major ~N-striking fault in bedrock, that has uplifted the Grampian Mountains that separate Hakatarmea valley from Mackenzie basin, with peneplain offset of as much as ~1000 m. No evidence for LQ offset, nominal slip rates assigned.

Name: Hunters
References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166) and refs therein
Comments: Name reverts to the long-standing term on geological maps and literature for this structure, 'Hunters Fault'. SR from Litchfield et al. 2014, rake revised to entertain small dextral component.

Name: Ostler South
References: Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166) and references therein; Amos et al. 2007, 2010, 2011
Comments: SR and dips from Litchfield et al. 2013. QC value of 2 reflects that despite limited direct investigation, excellent preservation of age-contrained fluvial surfaces across the fault provides evidence for recent tectonics.

Name: Falstone
Comments: Major fault in bedrock, with the Benmore Range showing as much as ~1200 m uplift of the peneplain to the southwest. Nominal slip rates inferred. Similarity of strike to Waitangi Fault forms basis for inferring possible dextral component

Name: Mt Sutton
References: Barrell CFM compilation
Comments: Major ~N-striking fault in bedrock, with uplift of unnamed range (highest point, Mt Sutton) northeast of the Aviemore basin.  There is no recognised Late Quaternary deformation, although rugged hill terrain reduces likelihood of its preservation.

Name: Dromedary
Comments: Previously Lindis Pass. ~5 m high scarp on inferred Holocene-age landforms pref SR 0.5 mm/yr, min SR of 0.1 mm/yr reflecting scarp could be single rupture,  max SR of 2x the pref, acknowledging uncertainties in scarp height and/or landform age inference

Name: Gibson
Comments: Major fault in bedrock, with uplift of unnamed range north of the Aviemore basin, with offset of the peneplain of typically as much as ~500 m. There is no recognised Late Quaternary deformation.

Name: Maungati
Comments: Recognition of LQ deformation and structural interpretation discussed in detail by Barrell (2016). Structural continuity with Brothers Fault is basis for assigning it the same SR as the Maungati Fault.

Name: Kirkliston
References: Barrell et al. 2008 (CR2007/146);  Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: Following the reasoning of Barrell 2016, the Kirkliston source is repositioned to the east side of the Mt MacGregor ridge, and now closely abut the south end of the Dalgety source

Name: Fern Gully
References: Barrell et al. 2002; Barrell et al. 2009 (GSNZ Misc Publ 128B);  Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: SR and dips from Litchfield et al. 2013. Minor revision to linework. QC value of 3 reflects that investigation has only been undertaken on a limited sector of the fault source, which includes a series of seperately named fault entities

Name: Campbell Hills
References: Barrell CFM compilation
Comments: Peneplain offset of typically ~500 m. There is no recognised Late Quaternary deformation, although rugged hill terrain reduces likelihood of its preservation. Nominal slip rates inferred.

Name: Waitangi
References: Barrell et al. 2002 (CR2001/125); Barrell et al. 2009 (GSNZ Misc Publ 128B);  Litchfield et al. 2013 (SR2012/19); Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: SR and dips from Litchfield et al. 2013. Note that this is a partially reactivated normal fault, hence the prominent topographic expression (higher to NE) is on the Late Quaternary kinematically downthrown side.

Name: Hawkdun
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Major fault in bedrock, up to 1 km Late Cenozoic peneplain offset. Blue Lake SR is applied to the Hawkdun Fault. No recognised Quaternary scarps, though in the mountain-front setting, conceivable no long-term recognisable surface evidence persists

Name: Dryburgh
References: Barrell et al. 2005 (CR2005/70); Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: Barrell et al. 2005 show evidence for no movement since at least 62 ka; low nominal slip rate (as for other 'no known activity' faults) assigned. Position of trace relocated to the SW to accord bett+AC137+AC85

Name: Middle Range
References: Retallack and Ryburn 1982; Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: This was formerly the Otematata fault source. Doubtful evidence for Late Quaternary movement; nominal slip rates applied

Name: Omarama Saddle
Comments: Inferred fault in bedrock, peneplain offset of several hundred metres. Definite fault scarp at N end of fault, and likely ones at far south end of fault. Barrell 2019 proposes 0.2 mm/yr SR, adopted here as pref. Nominal SR min/max

Name: Blue Lake
References: Henne et al. 2011 (NZJGG); Litchfield et al. 2013 (SR2012/019); Barrell 2019 (CR2018/207)
Comments: Major fault in bedrock, up to 1 km Late Cenozoic peneplain offset.  Barrell 2019 uses post-Miocene throw on peneplan to obtain SR of 0.07 mm/yr. This is porposes as pref. SR, with nominal min and max of 0.02 and 0.15 respectively.

Name: Awahokomo
References: Barrell et al. 2002 (CR2001/125); Barrell et al. 2009 (GSNZ Misc Publ 128B);  Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: SR from Litchfield et al. 2013; based on Barrell et al. (2002, 2009). Possible association with the SW-dipping Wharekuri Fault. QC of 3 reflects that investigation has only been undertaken at one location at the northern end of the fault source.

Name: Waimate
References: Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166) and references therein
Comments: Up up to 1 km Late Cenozoic throw.  Hunters Fault dips and rakes applied. Nominal slow SRs aplied. Lack of known deformation on relatively old fans and terraces is basis for slow SRs and QC of 4 in 100 ky timeframe

Name: Rocks Creek
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207); Beanland and Fellows 1985
Comments: Array of east-facing Quaternary fault scarps/monoclines, inferred association W-dipping bedrock fault. Interpred as a back-fault off Omaranma Saddle Fault; Barrell 2019 assigned SR as not independently rupturing structure.

Name: Stonewall
References: Barrell et al. 2004 (CR2004/56); Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: Max and min slip rates from younger and older bounds of most recent rupture documented by Barrell et al. 2005, with best rate being between those two values

Name: Black Hill
References: Barrell and Van Dissen 2003 (CR2003/107); Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: Major fault in bedrock, with as much as ~500 m offset of the peneplain, up to the southeast. Proposed as possible active fault by Barrell 2016. No definitive evidence for Late Quaternary movement, and nominal slip rates inferred.

Name: Waitaki
References: Barrell and Van Dissen 2003 (CR2003/107); Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: Major fault in bedrock, with as much as ~1200 m uplift of the peneplain to the southwest. There is no recognised Late Quaternary deformation, nominal slip rates inferred.

Name: Waihemo
Comments: Major fault in bedrock, up to 1 km reverse-fault movement to create Late Cenozoic peneplain offset. Barrell 2019 interprets a scarp on the Stranraer Fault near Naseby as related to Waihemo FZ rupture, and derives a 0.12 mm/yr SR pref

Name: Awamoa
Comments: Marine terrace height change (~7 m) is the main evidence for activity. Due to N-S strike, it is assessed as pure dip slip, and assigned a preferred slip rate of 0.1 mm/yr (9 m vertical offset since ~125 ka, resolved onto a 45 degree fault plane.

Name: Mistake - Rolleston
References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

Name: Mungo
References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

Name: Mathias
References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012

References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012

References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012

References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012

References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012

References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012

Name: Karangarua
References: Grindley 1960; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Villamor et al. 2001

Name: McKerrow - Douglas Duplex
References: Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014

Name: Great Groove
References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012

Name: Landsborough 2
References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Cox and Barrell 2007; Cox et al. 2012; Rattenbury et al. 2010

Name: Huxley
References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: Sourced from the Cox et al. 2012 interpretation, the fault as delineated in the NZAFM stepped across several fault structures, some identified as normal faults. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Hopkins
References: Barrell and Strong 2010 (CR2010/147); Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: 'Ahuriri' fault zone revision to 'Hopkins Fault'. Estimated scarp heights (5 to 10 m) on an inferred 18 ka land surface inform the slip rate estimates,

Name: Barrier Range
References: Litchfield et al. 2013; Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166)
Comments: Sourced from the Cox et al. 2012. Dobson revised to Barrier Range cf QMAP. Position refined to accord better with geological mapped location. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Wanaka
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Indicated fault(s) in bedrock; named 'Makarora Fault in NZAFM; for precedence, name reverts to Wanaka Fault (Turnbull 2000). Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps)

Name: Hunter Valley
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Indicated fault(s) in bedrock; Hunter Fault to Hunter Valley Fault (Turnbull 2000). Indicated post-glacial fault scarp. The min SR acknowledges single post-glacial rupture could account for the surface scarp, therefore SR unconstrained maximum

Name: Dingle
Comments: Dingle Burn' in NZAFM, name 'Dingle Fault' as used in QMAP datasets is applied here. General summit elevations either side of the line of the fault indicate NW-dipping reverse fault. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Moonlight North
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Refer to detailed description and dicussion in Barrell 2019a, regarding revised mapping of the north and south sectors of the Moonlight Fault, downgrading of its activity and slip rates

Name: Skippers
References: Ballard 1989; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Turnbull et al. 2010

Name: Hollyford
References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Sutherland 1995

Name: Livingstone
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Major fault in bedrock, indicated post-glacial offset; 'Livingstone Fault' used in preference to 'Livingstone Key Summit FZ'. Barrell 2019 SR of 1.0 mm/yr,reduced 50% as fault is not prominent across glacial landforms in upper Eglinton valley.

Name: West Wakatipu
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Major fault in bedrock; post-glacial scarps near Lake Wakatipu previously attributed to Moonlight Fault attributed to West Wakatipu Fault by Barrell 2019. Min and max SR vary by 50% from the preferred value

Name: Timaru Creek
Comments: Interpretation follows Barrell 2019. Estimated scarp heights of ~5 m on an inferred 18 ka land surface inform SR. The max SR allows that that scarp height, or landform age, could be up to 50% in error.

Name: Lindis River
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset; nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps)

Name: Grandview
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207), and references therein
Comments: pref SR of 0.1 mm/yr retained, as no surface rupture since ~30 ka but 80 m deformation of lake silts, of age estimate in range of ~150 ka to ~450 ka, 330 ka preferred (Barrell 2019).

Name: Goodger
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset; nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps)

Name: Paddys Ridge
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Formerly SE Cardrona Fault (Beanland and Barrow-Hurlbert 1988), the new name avoids possible confusion with the 'NW Cardona Fault' (Barrell 2019). Major fault in bedrock, peneplain offset; nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Cluden
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Faults in bedrock offsetting peneplain, and assessed monoclinal deformation of 'post-Lindis'-age lake silt. Formerly part of the 'Pisa' fault source, (e.g. Bealand and Berryman 1989) as the 'Lindis Peak' segment of the Pisa Fault,

Name: Dunstan
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207), and referencess therein; Van Dissen et al. 2007; Stirling et al. 2021
Comments: SW end lengthened slightly to approach the Old Man Fault. The Fish Creek and Cairnmuir faults are interpreted as abandoned strands of the Dunstan fault zone, and not regarded as independent fault sources

Name: Pisa
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207), and references therein; Beanland and Berryman 1989
Comments: End-points revised, shortened to north (see Cluden Fault Zone) and lengthened to south to include Carrick and Bannockburn fault strands; Pisa fault source positioned midway between those strands. NZAFM slip rates retained.

Name: Raggedy - Blackstone
References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207); Markley and Norris 1999; Markley and Tikoff 2003
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset. Proposed rename Raggedy to Raggedy-Blackstone, as used in the Barrrell 2019 which highlights geological name plus the seismic source name used subsequently.

Name: Garibaldi
References: Bishop 1979 (Ranfurly geol map); Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset of several hundred metres. NZAFM included in Gimmerburn, independent source is suggested here, given the fault's length, sizeable offset. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Gimmerburn
References: Bennett et al. 2005; Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014; Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Complex stepping fault zone; of the order of ~400 m offset of peneplain. Surface exposure dating implies ~60 m uplift since ~500 ka; uplift rate on 45 deg fault gives min SR of ~0.1 mm/yr. Preferred SR based on ~5 m scarp on estimate 18 ka fan

Name: Cross Eden
References: Bishop 1979 (Ranfurly geol map); Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, extrapolated south into Maniototo basin along topographic anomaly; also indicated in geophysics (Glass Earth). Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Ranfurly
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Comprises NNE-striking Launceston Fault, up to the W, and Ranfurly Fault Zone, a complex and wide array of ENE-striking fault scarps. Via inference Barrell 2019 assigned a 0.1 mm/yr SR, noting that scarp freshness implies Holocene rupture

Name: Waipiata
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Array of faults in bedrock, and monoclines in Cenzoic strata. Comprises NE Waipiata. Re-interpretations described by Barrell 2019. An inferred back-fault is interpreted to have deformed fluvial terraces of the Kye Burn valley. SR are nominal inferences.

Name: Hyde North
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88); Griffin (unpublished data)
Comments: Reconsideration of trench data interpretations by  Griffin (unpublished data) indicates ~6 m  net slip since ~23 ka, suggesting 0.25 mm/y best estimate. Max is 20% more, and min allows that the slip amount may be all that has occurred since ~65 ka.

Name: Galloway
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Array of faults in bedrock, peneplain offsets. Fault source near NW side of fault array (Blackmans Fault- Galloway Fault). Possible scarp on alluvial fan defines pref SR. Min SR recognises scarp may not be tectonic, max recognises difficult preservation

Name: Little Valley
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Array of faults in bedrock, peneplain offsets; typical peneplain throw across the array is ~300 m. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps). Source line positioned broadly along the middle of the array

Name: Galloway Shanty
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Inferred fault in bedrock; peneplain offset. Interpreted as a back-fault splay off the Galloway Fault Zone, and not an independent fault source

Name: Horse Flat
References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014;  Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166);  Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset ~150-200 m. Called Taieri Ridge Fault (Stirling et al 2012; Litchfield et al. 2013, Horse Flat Fault has precedence in literature (Barrell 2016, 2021). Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Long Valley
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset (up to ~300 m throw). Late Quaternary scarps collectively as much as ~8 m high on alluvial fans of inferred age. Barrell 2019a estimated 0.18 m pref SR, min SR nominal 0.05 mm/yr, max SR is 2x preferred

Name: Billys Ridge
References: Litchfield et al. 2013, 2014;  Barrell 2016 (CR2015/166);  Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset typically ~50-100 m but locally as much as 250 m (Barrell 2016). Includes Macraes Fault along strike to the northeast. No evidence for Late Quaternary movement, and nominal slip rates inferred.

Name: Pylap
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Inferred en-echelon faults in bedrock, peneplain offset ~50 m up to the SE. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Murphys Creek
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset as much as ~100 m (Barrell 2020). Identified as possible fault source by Villamor et al. 2018. No evidence for Late Quaternary movement, and nominal slip rates inferred.

Name: Dunback Hill
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset  typically ~50-100 m but locally as much as 150 m (Barrell 2020). No evidence for Late Quaternary movement, and nominal slip rates inferred.

Name: Lake Onslow
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Inferred fault in bedrock, peneplain offset, ~100 m up to the west. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Flat Stream - Glenpark
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Fault(s) in bedrock, peneplain offset  typically ~50-100 m but locally as much as 200 m (Barrell 2020). No recognised evidence for Late Quaternary movement, and nominal slip rates inferred.

Name: Logan Burn
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Inferred fault in bedrock, peneplain offset, as much as ~350 m up to the southeast. Comprises SW Waipiata. Re-interpretations described by Barrell 2019. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Beaumont River
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Inferred fault in bedrock, peneplain offset, as much as ~200 m up to the east. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Sliver Stream - Merton
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Barrell 2019 lengthened the west end, as per above; overall length increased ~6 km

Name: Hyde South - The Twins
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88); Griffin (unpublished data)
Comments: Hyde_south corresponds to 'The Twins moncline' described by Barrell 2020. Best slip rate is 50% of the Hyde north rate, as discussed by Barrell 2020. Classified N-PS due to lack of direct evidence for LQ surface deformation

Name: Backbone
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Inferred fault in bedrock, peneplain offset, as much as ~200 m up to the west. Nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Nichols Rock
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Inferred monocline in bedrock, based on indicated deformation of peneplain . Along strike of termination of Flat Stream Fault. No evidence for or against Late Quaternary deformation. Nominal slip rates inferred.

Name: Titri North
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88); Barrell et al. 2020 (SR2017/35); Litchfield 2001
Comments: Currently drawn as three segments, as per Barrell et al. (2020).

Name: Maungatua - North Taieri
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Barrell 2020 used term Waipori-Maungatua-North Taieri Fault to more clearly reflect its geologically-mapped component structures, but simplified Maungatua-North Taieri Fault retained as a fault source name (as used by Villamor et al. 2018).

Name: Kaikorai
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Barrell 2020 suggestion that it is a splay off the Titri and not an independent fault source. For the moment, it is assigned the nominal SR (0.05 pref) applied to other faults of doubtful activity

Name: Waitahuna 1
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: NE limit shortened to allow extension of Waipori Fault; SW end lengthened, about the same net length

Name: Takapu
References: Goded et al. 2019 (CR2019/79)

Name: Green Island
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124)
Comments: Barrell 2020 suggested that recency of trace on GIF suggests association with Holocene Akatore rupture (triggered?). Holocene net amount (4.8 to 7.4 m - median 6.1 m) from Taylor-Silva et al. 2020 applied over 5 ka timeframe.

Name: Waitahuna 2
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88)
Comments: Shortened to allow extension of Waipori Fault; Barrell 2019 proposes as a splay of the No. 1 fault, not an independent source

Name: Titri Central
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88); Barrell et al. 2020 (SR2017/35); Litchfield 2001
Comments: Currently drawn as three segments, as per Barrell et al. (2020).

Name: Akatore
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Holt 2017; Taylor-Silva et al. 2020; Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88); Craw et al. 2020; Litchfield and Norris 2000
Comments: Barrell 2020 suggested that recency of trace on Green Island Fault suggests association with Holocene Akatore rupture (triggered?). Holocene net amount (4.8 to 7.4 m - median 6.1 m) from Taylor-Silva et al. 2020 applied over 5 ka timeframe.

Name: Titri South
References: Villamor et al. 2018 (GNS MS 124); Barrell 2021 (CR2020/88); Barrell et al. 2020 (SR2017/35); Litchfield 2001
Comments: Currently drawn as three segments, as per Barrell et al. (2020).

Name: Motatapu
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: A N-S array of fault scarps in the 'Cardrona' range, called the Highland Fault, is interpreted as a splay of the Motatapu Fault (Barrell 2019). Preferred SR is from surface scarps of assumed post-glacial age.

Name: Cardrona - Hawea
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Formerly northwest end NW Cardrona Fault. Fault in bedrock, but no recognisable post-glacial surface deformation. Nominal preferred SR of 0.05 mm/yr, min SR of 0.025 acknowledges proximity to Quaternery-active faults

Name: NW Cardrona North
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207); van den Berg 2020; Beanland and Barrow-Hurlbert 1988
Comments: 2-segment model of NSHM retained, but fault lengths and end-positions altered. Recalculated age data from Bealand and Barrow Hurlbert (1988) indicate a max SR of 0.2 at Kawarau valley, and post-glacial monocline deformation at Wanaka implies ~0.3 mm/yr

Name: NW Cardrona South
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207); van den Berg 2020
Comments: 2-segment model of NSHM retained, but fault lengths and end-positions altered. Recalculated age data from Bealand and Barrow Hurlbert (1988) indicate a max SR of 0.2 at Kawarau valley, and post-glacial monocline deformation at Wanaka implies ~0.3 mm/yr

Name: Roaring Meg
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Equates in part ot 'Gentle Annie Fault' of Beanland and Barrow-Hurlbert 1988, as explained by Barrell 2019. Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset; nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps).

Name: Nevis
References: Beanland and Barrow-Hurlbert 1988; Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: The max SR only slightly more than preferred SR (0.4; from NSHM/NZAFM) indicates that preferred SR is likely to be close to a maximum. Barrell 2019 raises possibility of segmented rupture based on small single event displacements.

Name: Moonlight South
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Refer to detailed description and discussion in Barrell 2019a, regarding revised mapping of the north and south sectors of the Moonlight Fault, downgrading of its activity and slip rates. Southern limit placed at north end of Takitimu Mountains

Name: Roaring Lion
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset; nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps)

Name: Old Man
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Slip rates revised from NSHM/NZAFM; preferred SR uses adopted age of 'Lindis Gravel', max and min assume age differs by 50% from that estimate

Name: Garvie
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, peneplain offset; nominal slip rates inferred (no known Late Quaternary scarps)

Name: Waikaia
References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); Barrell CFM compilation
Comments: Represents an en-cechelon array of fault slices, that uplift basement to the E against Tertiary strata by many hundreds of metres. No reported evidence for Late Q deformation, nominal slip rates applied.

Name: Acton
References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); Barrell CFM compilation
Comments: Connects Late Q scarps on Five Rivers Plain and fault scarp up Acton Stream, shown on QMAP. Approx 2 m scarp on ~18 ka surface basis for slip rates, plus topographic expression (up to E) in hill country.

Name: Mid Dome
References: Barrell CFM compilation
Comments: Inferred to account for prominent elevation of the Mid Dome ridge, up to ~1 km throw on peneplain.  Nominal slip rates, mod-steep east dip, and some movement obliquity inferred.

Name: Teviot
References: Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Fault in bedrock, indicated peneplain offset; slip rates adopted from adjacent Old Man Fault

Name: Wendon Valley
References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); Barrell CFM compilation
Comments: This source is sub-parallel to the Waikaia source. Name is from QMAP, throw has uplifted the Black Umbrella Range, by hundreds of metres relative to Tertiary outliers. No reported evidence for Late Q deformation, nominal slip rates applied.

Name: McKerchar
References: Turnbull and Allibone 2003 (QMAP); Carter and Norris 2005 (SR2004/23); Barrell 2019a (CR2018/207)
Comments: Referred to by Cater and Norris as 'Takitimu Boundary Fault Zone'; complex fault zone. Remanent Quat scarps. Accounts for main uplift of Takitimu Mountains. Fault dips and rake is guess. Scarps on old fans give slip rate estimates (see Barrell 2019)
